claims.text: The coupled tribo-corrosion response of high-entropy alloys is dominated by a dynamic balance between passive-film removal by wear and rapid passive-film reformation.
Fe20Co20Ni20Mn20Cu20 is an equimolar high-entropy-alloy composition.
The proposed initial Fe20Co20Ni20Mn20Cu20 material is homogeneous.
The initial alloy possesses a uniform, self-assembled passive oxide layer.
Mechanical sliding disrupts and removes the protective oxide film at contact sites.
Compromise or breach of an oxide or protective coating in chloride solution enables localized corrosion such as pitting or crevice corrosion.
Fresh alloy exposed by wear undergoes accelerated electrochemical attack by chloride ions.
High configurational entropy intrinsically promotes rapid oxide regeneration.
The uniform distribution of multiple elements and the alloy's grain-boundary characteristics mediate passive-film integrity and regeneration kinetics.
Rapid in situ formation of a new protective oxide after wear limits further degradation.
Improving passive-film stability can improve corrosion resistance in a high-entropy-alloy coating.
Simultaneous tribo-corrosion will produce increased pit density and oxidation beneath or near wear tracks.
Simultaneous tribo-corrosion will cause a moderately higher overall degradation rate than either wear-only or corrosion-only exposure.
Rapid oxide reformation will make total material loss lower than in conventional alloys.
During corrosion-only testing, the passive film remains largely intact.
The proposed behavior should hold when passive-film formation kinetics are competitive with the rate of wear.
The mechanism may fail under extreme mechanical loads, in low-oxygen environments, or for alloys that do not form robust passive films.
A controlled experiment can vary oxide-reformation capability while holding bulk composition, microstructure, electrolyte, and wear conditions constant.
Failure of inhibited-reformation samples to show significantly greater localized corrosion and overall degradation would falsify the proposed mitigation mechanism.

contradictions.description: The experiment specifies identical bulk compositions but offers introduction of a dopant as one way to inhibit oxide reformation; a dopant would generally alter composition and could also alter microstructure, undermining the stated matched comparison.
